nodes.text: Welcome to the artisans' hall — looms left, carving right, commissions by appointment, opinions free of charge. I'm Ottilie. Mind the thread tension; it's set finer than most tempers.

choices.text: Where does mountain cloth come from?

nodes.text: Every one. The Warden asked for 'something dignified' and I delivered dignity with one thread of arrogance woven through the field — silver on silver, visible only when the hall fires gutter. Twenty years and nobody's spotted it. Maren would approve, which is why I'll never tell her.

Lowland cotton up the High Road, mountain wool off Ivo's neighbors' rams, and lately gloomsilk thread out of the deep — the spiders below spin finer than anything under the sun, which is the sort of sentence my trade makes you say with a straight face. Weaving is just weather, organized. Down there it's darkness, organized. The loom doesn't care.
Bolts and thread, mountain grade. If it frays before the year turns, bring it back and watch me not believe you.
